Histidine at position 28 cannot make the contacts the arginine makes across the dimer interface, so the dimer does not form and BTK activation at the membrane is impaired.","supports":["E6","E8","E1","E2","E9"],"would_refute":"Modelled or experimental PH-TH dimer structures place residue 28 with no atom within contact distance (about 4 Å) of the partner chain, and the R28H model keeps the interface buried area and interface energy within the wild-type range.","latest_verdict":"untested","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"},{"id":"H2","mechanism_class":"ligand_binding","starting_rank":2,"statement":"R28H removes a side-chain contact that BTK's PH domain uses to bind the inositol phosphate head group (IP4 or IP6). The loss of that contact weakens ligand recognition and membrane targeting.","supports":["E5","E12","E16","E15","E10"],"would_refute":"In ligand-bound experimental structures (1B55 with 4IP), residue 28 has no atom within about 4 Å of the bound inositol phosphate, and the R28H model shows a binding free energy to Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 within the wild-type range.","latest_verdict":"untested","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"},{"id":"H3","mechanism_class":"stability_folding","starting_rank":3,"statement":"R28H destabilises the PH domain fold, through loss of buried packing or a polar network near residue 28, so the domain is partly unfolded or underexpressed.
